content: To determine the total number of lymphedema patients, it is essential to sum the total number of lymphedema patients reported in the previous reporting period (Question 1) with the number of new lymphedema cases identified during the current reporting period (Question 2). Similarly, to calculate the total number of known hydrocele patients, the total number of hydrocele patients from the previous reporting period (Question 4) must be added to the number of new hydrocele cases identified during the current reporting period (Question 5). The reporting period should be clearly defined using the format DD/MM/YYYY to DD/MM/YYYY. The name of the community health worker responsible for the data collection, the communities they serve, and the name of the health center must also be documented. For lymphedema, the following data points should be recorded: 1. The total number of lymphedema patients under the responsibility of the community health worker. 2. The number of new lymphedema patients identified during the reporting period. 3. The number of patients receiving lymphedema or ADL (Activities of Daily Living) care, which includes initial consultations, follow-up visits, ADL management visits, and psychological services. For hydrocele (scrotal swelling), the following data points should be recorded: 1. The total number of known hydrocele patients. 2. The number of new hydrocele cases identified during the reporting period. 3. The number of patients referred for hydrocele-related care. 4. The number of patients who underwent hydrocelectomy surgery. Each health center providing MMDP (Morbidity Management and Disability Prevention) services must complete a reporting form for submission to the appropriate implementation unit authority. This form should summarize data submitted by community health workers, if applicable, and include the number of patients and those receiving care at both the community and health facility levels. At the implementation unit level, a summary of data from all health centers providing MMDP care should be compiled and submitted to the national level, either directly or through a regional level. This report should include the total number of health facilities in the implementation unit, the number providing lymphedema/ADL services, and the number providing hydrocele services. At the national level, an annual report should be submitted to the Global Programme to Eliminate Lymphatic Filariasis (GPELF). This report should include data extracted from the EPI Reporting Form (EPIRF) and provide a comprehensive summary of MMDP data. Further details can be found in the web annex.
